metadata.title: Quasiorders on Topological Categories
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: metadata.json lists this paper as 'The Parisi Formula' by Talagrand (2006), but the actual PDF/text content is 'Quasiorders on Topological Categories' by Věra Trnková, Proceedings of the Ninth Prague Topological Symposium (2002), arXiv:math/0204143. Extraction reflects the actual PDF content.

nodes.name: Quasiorder induced by a class of morphisms
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a class of morphisms of a category $\mathcal{K}$ containing all isomorphisms and closed under composition. Then $\mathcal{M}$ determines a quasiorder $\preceq$ on objects of $\mathcal{K}$ by: $X \preceq Y$ iff there exists $m \in \mathcal{M}$ with domain $X$ and codomain $Y$.
nodes.statement_clean: A class of morphisms closed under composition and containing isomorphisms induces a quasiorder on objects: X precedes Y iff some morphism in the class maps X to Y.

nodes.name: $\mathcal{M}$-representation of a quasiordered set
nodes.statement: An $\mathcal{M}$-representation of a quasiordered set $(Q, \leq)$ in $\mathcal{K}$ is a collection $\mathcal{X} = \{X(q) : q \in Q\}$ of non-isomorphic objects of $\mathcal{K}$ such that for every $q, q' \in Q$: $q \leq q'$ iff $X(q) \preceq X(q')$.
nodes.statement_clean: A representation assigns each quasiorder element a non-isomorphic object so that the order on Q matches the morphism-induced order on objects.

nodes.name: Sum-productive representation of a partially ordered commutative semigroup
nodes.statement: For $(S, \circ, \leq)$ a partially ordered commutative semigroup, a sum-productive representation in category $\mathcal{K}$ is a collection $\{X(s): s \in S\}$ such that (×) $X(s \circ s')$ is isomorphic to the product $X(s) \times X(s')$, and ($\leq$) $s \leq s'$ iff $X(s)$ is isomorphic to a summand of $X(s')$.
nodes.statement_clean: A representation that turns the semigroup operation into a categorical product and the order into the summand relation.

nodes.name: Cited result of Kuratowski and Sierpiński (1926)
nodes.statement: The antichain of cardinality $2^{\mathfrak{c}}$ and the ordinal $\mathfrak{c}^{+}$ have $\mathcal{M}$-representations within the category of all subspaces of the real line $\mathbb{R}$, where $\mathcal{M}$ is the class of homeomorphic embeddings.
nodes.statement_clean: Antichains of size 2^c and the ordinal c^+ embed as subspaces of the real line under homeomorphic embedding.

nodes.name: Matthews–McMaster representation theorem
nodes.statement: Every partially ordered set of cardinality $\mathfrak{c}$ has a representation by subspaces of $\mathbb{R}$ with respect to the embeddability.
nodes.statement_clean: Posets of size c can be represented inside the real line by embeddability.

nodes.name: McCluskey–McMaster–Watson theorem on $(\exp \mathbb{R}, \subseteq)$
nodes.statement: The set $(\exp \mathbb{R}, \subseteq)$ of all subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ ordered by inclusion has a representation by subspaces of $\mathbb{R}$ with respect to the embeddability.
nodes.statement_clean: The full power set of R, ordered by inclusion, embeds inside R itself by embeddability of subspaces.

nodes.name: McCluskey–McMaster representation in $T_3$-spaces
nodes.statement: For infinite cardinals $a, b$ with $b^a = b$, every partially ordered set $(P, \leq)$ with $|P| \leq b$ has a representation (with respect to embeddability) by subsets of every $T_3$-space $X$ containing a dense subset $D$ with $|D| \leq a$, provided every non-empty open set of $X$ has cardinality $b$.
nodes.statement_clean: Posets bounded by b embed as subsets of any sufficiently rich T3-space when the cardinal arithmetic b^a = b holds.
assumptions: $X$ is a $T_3$-space with a dense subset $D$ of cardinality $|D| \leq a$
every non-empty open set of $X$ has cardinality $b$
conclusions: $(P, \leq)$ has a representation by subsets of $X$ with respect to embeddability

nodes.name: McCluskey–McMaster $T_0$-space construction
nodes.statement: Given a cardinal $\alpha$, there exists a $T_0$-space $X$ with $|X| = \delta(\alpha)$ such that every quasiordered set $(Q, \leq)$ with $|Q| \leq \alpha$ has a representation by subsets of $X$ (with respect to embeddability), where $\delta(\alpha)$ is the smallest cardinal $\delta$ with $\alpha$ distinct cardinals smaller than $\delta$.
nodes.statement_clean: There is a T0-space whose subsets represent every quasiordered set of size up to alpha.

nodes.name: Vinárek’s sum-productive representation theorem
nodes.statement: Every partially ordered commutative semigroup has a sum-productive representation in the category of all metric zero-dimensional spaces.
nodes.statement_clean: Every poset commutative semigroup is sum-productively representable by metric zero-dimensional spaces.

nodes.name: Pultr–Trnková rigid system of metrizable spaces
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha \geq \mathfrak{c}$ there exists a system $\mathcal{S}$ of metrizable spaces of cardinality $\alpha$ (with $|\mathcal{S}| = \alpha$, in fact $|\mathcal{S}| = 2^{\alpha}$ is achievable) such that for every $Y, Z \in \mathcal{S}$ and every continuous map $f : Y \to Z$, either $f$ is constant or $Y = Z$ and $f$ is the identity.
nodes.statement_clean: There is a large rigid family of metrizable spaces in which the only continuous maps between members are constants or identities.

nodes.name: Ketonen-type Cantor subset
nodes.statement: There exists a closed subset $K$ of the Cantor discontinuum such that $K$ is homeomorphic to $K \sqcup K \sqcup K$ but not to $K \sqcup K$.
nodes.statement_clean: There is a closed subset of the Cantor set isomorphic to three disjoint copies of itself but not to two.

nodes.name: Main theorem: simultaneous representation of paired quasiorders by clopen subspaces
nodes.statement: For every cardinal $\alpha \geq \mathfrak{c}$, there exists a metrizable space $X$ with $|X| = \alpha$ such that for every pair $\leq_1, \leq_2$ of quasiorders on a set $Q$ with $|Q| \leq \alpha$ satisfying $q \leq_1 q' \Rightarrow q \leq_2 q'$, there exists a system $\{X(q): q \in Q\}$ of non-homeomorphic clopen subsets of $X$ realizing $\leq_1$ as homeomorphism-to-clopen-subset, $\leq_2$ as homeomorphism-to-closed-subset, and $\neg(q \leq_2 q')$ as non-existence of one-to-one continuous maps.
nodes.statement_clean: A single metrizable space whose clopen subspaces simultaneously represent any compatible pair of quasiorders by clopen and closed embeddings.
assumptions: $\leq_1, \leq_2$ are quasiorders on $Q$ with $q \leq_1 q' \Rightarrow q \leq_2 q'$
conclusions: There exists a metrizable space $X$ with $|X| = \alpha$
There exists a system $\{X(q): q \in Q\}$ of non-homeomorphic clopen subsets of $X$
$q \leq_1 q'$ iff $X(q)$ is homeomorphic to a clopen subset of $X(q')$
$q \leq_2 q'$ implies $X(q)$ is homeomorphic to a closed subset of $X(q')$
$\neg(q \leq_2 q')$ implies no one-to-one continuous map of $X(q)$ into $X(q')$

nodes.name: Two-condition $\mathcal{M}$-representation by retracts
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha \geq \mathfrak{c}$ there exists a metrizable space $X$ with $|X| = \alpha$ such that every quasiordered set $(Q, \leq)$ with $|Q| \leq \alpha$ has an $\mathcal{M}$-representation by retracts of $X$ whenever (1) $\mathcal{M}$ consists of one-to-one continuous maps and contains all coproduct injections, or (2) $\mathcal{M}$ consists of continuous surjections and contains all product projections.
nodes.statement_clean: A single metrizable space whose retracts represent every quasiordered set under either of two natural choices of morphism class.

nodes.name: Representation by clopen subspaces via continuous bijections
nodes.statement: For every cardinal $\alpha \geq \mathfrak{c}$ there exists a metrizable space $X$ with $|X| = \alpha$ such that every quasiordered set $(Q, \leq)$ with $|Q| \leq \alpha$ has an $\mathcal{M}$-representation by clopen subspaces of $X$, where $\mathcal{M}$ is the class of all continuous bijections.
nodes.statement_clean: Adding alpha isolated points to each X(q) yields a representation under continuous bijections.

nodes.name: Representation of posets by zero-dimensional metrizable spaces
nodes.statement: Every partially ordered set has a representation by zero-dimensional metrizable spaces with respect to the embeddability onto clopen subspaces.
nodes.statement_clean: Every poset is representable inside zero-dimensional metric spaces by clopen embeddings.

nodes.name: Representation of $(\exp C, \subseteq)$ for countable $C$
nodes.statement: If $C$ is a countable set, then $(\exp C, \subseteq)$ has a representation by $F_{\sigma\delta}$ and $G_{\sigma\delta}$ subspaces of the Cantor discontinuum with respect to the embeddability onto clopen subspaces.
nodes.statement_clean: The power set of a countable set, ordered by inclusion, embeds in the Cantor set via clopen subspaces of certain Borel classes.

nodes.name: Existence of auxiliary systems $S^{(1)},\dots,S^{(4)}$
nodes.statement: Suppose $S^{(1)}, \dots, S^{(4)}$ are sets of metrizable spaces with $|S^{(i)}| = \alpha$ and $|Y| = \alpha$ for every $Y \in S^{(i)}$, satisfying conditions (1)–(5): mutually rigid systems exhibiting prescribed clopen/closed embeddability relations between paired members $\{A_q, B_q\}, \{D_q, E_q\}, \{M_q, N_q\}, \{G_q, H_q\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standing assumption that four families of metrizable spaces exist, each with carefully prescribed mutual embeddability properties.

nodes.name: Construction of the master space $X$
nodes.statement: $X = \bigsqcup_{q \in Q} (A_q \sqcup B_q \sqcup (D_q \times \omega) \sqcup (E_q \times \omega) \sqcup M_q \sqcup N_q \sqcup G_q)$, where $\sqcup$ denotes coproduct (disjoint union as clopen subspaces) and $\omega$ is a countable discrete space.
nodes.statement_clean: X is the coproduct over q in Q of the seven auxiliary pieces.

nodes.name: Auxiliary partial order $<$ on $Q$
nodes.statement: Define $q < q'$ iff $(q \leq_1 q')$ and $\neg(q' \leq_1 q)$ and $(q' \leq_2 q)$. Set $q \leq q'$ iff $q < q'$ or $q = q'$. Under (2.1), $\leq$ is a partial order.
nodes.statement_clean: An auxiliary partial order combining strict <_1 with the reverse <_2 relation.

nodes.name: Components $\mathcal{C}$ of $\leq$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{C}$ is the system of all components of $\leq$: $q, q' \in C \in \mathcal{C}$ iff there exist $q_0, \dots, q_n$ in $Q$ with $q = q_0 \leq q_1 \geq q_2 \leq \dots q_n = q'$.
nodes.statement_clean: Components are equivalence classes generated by alternating chains in the auxiliary order.

nodes.name: Stage-1 spaces $X_q^{(1)}$
nodes.statement: For $q \in C \in \mathcal{C}$ put $S_q^{(1)} = \{B_{q'} : q' \leq q\} \cup \{A_{q'} : q' \in C \text{ and } \neg(q' \leq q)\}$ and $X_q^{(1)} = \bigsqcup S_q^{(1)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Each X_q^(1) is a coproduct of B-pieces below q and A-pieces incomparable with q in its component.

nodes.name: Relation $R$ and its transitive closure $\preceq$
nodes.statement: Define $q R q'$ iff either $q < q'$, or ($q \leq_2 q'$ and $q' \leq_2 q$ but neither $q \leq_1 q'$ nor $q' \leq_1 q$). Let $\prec$ be the transitive envelope of $R$ and $\preceq$ mean $\prec$ or $=$.
nodes.statement_clean: R combines the strict order with mutual <_2-equivalence outside <_1, and ≼ is its reflexive transitive closure.

nodes.name: Stage-2 spaces $X_q^{(2)}$
nodes.statement: For $q \in C \in \mathcal{C}$ with $C \subseteq L$, $S_q^{(2)} = S_q^{(1)} \cup \bigcup_{C' \in \mathcal{C}, C \neq C' \subseteq L}(B_{C'} \cup E_{C'} \cup D_{C'}) \cup E_C$ and $X_q^{(2)} = \bigsqcup S_q^{(2)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: X_q^(2) augments X_q^(1) with B-, D-, E-pieces from sibling components in the same L-component plus E_C.

nodes.name: Relation $\dot{R}$ and components $\mathcal{T}$
nodes.statement: Define $q \dot{R} q'$ iff $q \prec q'$ or $q \neq q', q \leq_1 q'$ or $q \neq q', q \leq_2 q'$. Let $\dot{\prec}$ be its transitive envelope and $\dot{\preceq}$ mean $\dot{\prec}$ or $=$. Let $\mathcal{T}$ be the system of components of $\dot{\preceq}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A coarser relation merging ≺ with the original quasiorders, with components T classifying the entire Q.

nodes.name: Final spaces $X(q)$
nodes.statement: For $q \in L$, $S_q^{(3)} = \widetilde{S}_q^{(2)} \cup \{N_{q'} : q' \in T \text{ and } q' \leq_1 q\} \cup \{M_{q'} : q' \in T \text{ and } \neg(q' \leq_1 q)\}$, and $X(q) = \bigsqcup S_q^{(3)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Final X(q) augments stage-2 spaces with M/N-pieces over the T-component encoding the <_1 relation.

nodes.name: Proof of the Main Theorem
nodes.statement: By a multi-stage construction: Part A assumes existence of auxiliary rigid systems $S^{(1)}\dots S^{(4)}$ and uses them to build $\{X(q)\}$ realizing the required embeddability relations; Part B constructs the systems $S^{(1)}\dots S^{(4)}$ from a Pultr–Trnková rigid family.
nodes.statement_clean: Two-part proof: assume the auxiliary systems and use them to build the representation, then construct the systems explicitly.

nodes.name: Set up auxiliary systems and master space
nodes.statement: Assume existence of $S^{(1)}, \dots, S^{(4)}$ satisfying conditions (1)–(5). Define $X$ as the coproduct $\bigsqcup_{q\in Q}(A_q \sqcup B_q \sqcup (D_q\times\omega) \sqcup (E_q\times\omega) \sqcup M_q \sqcup N_q \sqcup G_q)$.

nodes.name: Reduce to the case $\leq_1$ a partial order
nodes.statement: Suppose first that $\leq_1$ satisfies (2.1), i.e. $(q \leq_1 q')$ and $(q' \leq_1 q) \Rightarrow q = q'$, so $\leq_1$ is a partial order. The general quasiorder case is recovered at the end via passage to $Q/\sim$.

nodes.name: Build stage-1 spaces $X_q^{(1)}$ via $S^{(1)}$ and components $\mathcal{C}$
nodes.statement: Define $<$ and the components $\mathcal{C}$ of $\leq$. For each $q \in C \in \mathcal{C}$ define $X_q^{(1)} = \bigsqcup(\{B_{q'}: q' \leq q\} \cup \{A_{q'}: q' \in C, \neg(q' \leq q)\})$. Verify the observation that $q < q'$ iff $X_q^{(1)}$ is clopen in $X_{q'}^{(1)}$ and $X_{q'}^{(1)}$ is closed but not clopen in $X_q^{(1)}$.

nodes.name: Build stage-2 spaces $X_q^{(2)}$ via $S^{(2)}$ and components $\mathcal{L}$
nodes.statement: Define $R$ and its transitive envelope $\preceq$ with components $\mathcal{L}$. For $q \in C \subseteq L$, set $X_q^{(2)} = \bigsqcup(S_q^{(1)} \cup \bigcup_{C' \subseteq L, C \neq C'}(B_{C'} \cup E_{C'} \cup D_{C'}) \cup E_C)$. Verify that $\{X_q^{(2)}: q \in L\}$ realizes $\leq_1$ via clopen embedding and $\leq_2$ via closed embedding within each $L$-component.

nodes.name: Augment via $S^{(3)}$ to obtain final $X(q)$
nodes.statement: Define $\dot{R}, \dot{\preceq}$ with components $\mathcal{T}$. Set $\widetilde{S}_q^{(2)} = S_q^{(2)} \cup \bigcup_{L' \dot{\prec} L} \widetilde{S}_{L'}^{(2)}$ and $X(q) = \bigsqcup(\widetilde{S}_q^{(2)} \cup \{N_{q'}: q' \leq_1 q\} \cup \{M_{q'}: \neg(q' \leq_1 q)\})$. Check that adding M/N summands does not destroy intra-$L$ relations and supplies the missing $\leq_1$-encoding when $q \leq_2 q'$ and $\neg(q' \leq_1 q)$.

nodes.name: Case analysis across components
nodes.statement: Verify properties for $q_1, q_2 \in Q$: case $q_1, q_2 \in L$ done above; case $q_1 \in T, q_2 \in T'$ distinct gives no continuous one-to-one map, matching $\neg(q_1 \leq_2 q_2)$ and $\neg(q_2 \leq_2 q_1)$; case distinct $L_1, L_2$ within the same $T$ splits into ($\alpha$) $L_1, L_2$ incomparable in $\dot{\preceq}$ and ($\beta$) $L_1 \dot{\prec} L_2$.

nodes.name: Remove the partial-order assumption (2.1) using $S^{(4)}$
nodes.statement: Define $q \sim q'$ iff $q \leq_1 q'$ and $q' \leq_1 q$. On $Q/\sim$, $\leq_1$ is a partial order. Construct $S_{[q]}^{(3)}$ for each class. For $q \in [q]$, set $S_q^{(3)} = S_{[q]}^{(3)} \cup \{G_{q'}: q' \in Q \setminus \{q\}\} \cup \{H_q\}$ and $X_q = \bigsqcup S_q^{(3)}$, exploiting condition (4) on $\{G_q, H_q\}$.

nodes.name: Construct $S^{(1)}$ from rigid family
nodes.statement: From a subsystem $\{A_q^*, D_q^*, E_q^*, M_q^*, G_q^*: q \in Q\}$ of the rigid family $\mathcal{S}$, choose distinct points $a_q, b_q \in A_q^*$, in $A_q^* \times \omega$ identify $(b_q, n)$ with $(a_q, n+1)$ to form $A_q$, and put $B_q = A_q^* \sqcup A_q$. Then $S^{(1)} = \{A_q, B_q\}$ satisfies (1).

nodes.name: Construct $S^{(2)}$
nodes.statement: Choose two distinct points $d_q^{(1)}, d_q^{(2)} \in D_q^*$ and $e_q^{(1)}, e_q^{(2)} \in E_q^*$; in $D_q^* \times \omega$ identify $(d_q^{(2)}, n)$ with $(d_q^{(1)}, n+1)$ to obtain $\widetilde{D}_q$; analogously $\widetilde{E}_q$. Put $D_q = D_q^* \sqcup \widetilde{D}_q \sqcup \widetilde{E}_q$ and $E_q = E_q^* \sqcup \widetilde{D}_q \sqcup \widetilde{E}_q$. Then $S^{(2)}$ satisfies (2).

nodes.name: Construct $S^{(3)}$
nodes.statement: Construct $M_q$ and $N_q$ from $M_q^*$ exactly as $A_q, B_q$ from $A_q^*$ in step 8. Then $S^{(3)} = \{M_q, N_q\}$ satisfies (3).

nodes.name: Construct $S^{(4)}$ via Ketonen subset
nodes.statement: Let $K$ be a closed subset of the Cantor discontinuum with $K \cong K \sqcup K \sqcup K$ but $K \not\cong K \sqcup K$ ([4]). Put $G_q = K \times G_q^*$ and $H_q = (K \sqcup K) \times G_q^*$. Then $G_q$ is clopen-embeddable in $H_q$ and vice versa but they are non-homeomorphic, satisfying (4).

nodes.name: Verify cross-system rigidity (5)
nodes.statement: Since $\{A_q^*, D_q^*, E_q^*, M_q^*, N_q^*, G_q^*: q \in Q\} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ and the latter is rigid (only constant or identity continuous maps between members), $S^{(1)} \cup S^{(2)} \cup S^{(3)} \cup S^{(4)}$ inherits property (5) automatically.

nodes.name: No isolated points in $X(q)$
nodes.statement: Inspecting the proof, none of the spaces $X(q)$ has an isolated point. Adding $\alpha$ isolated points to every $X(q)$ (and to $X$) yields the corollary about continuous bijections.

nodes.name: Companion result on continuous surjections deferred
nodes.statement: The proof of claim (2) of the introductory proposition (representability via continuous surjections containing all product projections) and its stronger pair-of-quasiorders variant are not given here and will appear elsewhere.

nodes.name: Open questions on representability by special subspace classes
nodes.statement: Which quasiordered sets can be represented by metrizable zero-dimensional spaces, or by closed/Borelian/all subsets of the real line, with respect to the embeddability onto clopen/Borelian/closed subspaces or onto retracts?
